title: add transactional downgrade guard + backup/restore + schema migrations for private-installer
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Customers running Redwood Private need safe, automated upgrades for on-prem/VPC installs. Upgrades that change Postgres schema are high risk: failures can leave clusters in inconsistent states and make downgrades impossible. This PR implements a transactional downgrade guard and end-to-end backup/restore + schema migration tooling for the private-installer so upgrades can be tested, rolled back, and gated automatically.

What this changes: - Transactional migrations: introduce a migration runner that groups schema changes into atomic steps and records an idempotent migration_plan with forward and (when possible) generated downgrade SQL. Migration runner runs inside a Kubernetes job with a pre-check and post-check. - Downgrade guard: before applying migrations the installer writes a downgrade_guard record to the installation state bucket and cluster (migration plan, checksum, applied_at). During upgrade/rollback the guard verifies that the plan has a validated downgrade path; if not, the installer requires manual approval via the CLI/console. - Backup/restore: add pre-upgrade snapshot step using pg_dump + wal shipping to configurable object storage (S3/GCS) and an automatic verification run that restores the dump into a disposable test namespace and runs a smoke-check suite. - Helm hooks & charts: add helm pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks to create a migration lock (ConfigMap) and run the migration Job. Hooks are configurable via values (enableTransactionalMigrations=true). - Version pinning: surface explicit chart and imageTag pinning in installer manifests so operator can enforce exact versions for safe rollbacks. - Terraform changes: add optional backup_bucket config and IAM policy snippets to private-installer terraform module; document retention and lifecycle rules. - CLI: add installer migrate --dry-run and installer rollback --verify commands to the private-installer CLI to surface migration plans and run restore verification. - Tests: add integration harness to run a full upgrade -> verify -> rollback flow in CI (runs on smaller Postgres instance).

Why: This reduces upgrade risk for enterprise customers that require guaranteed rollback paths and audited backups for compliance. It also allows automated canary & staged upgrades with enforced verification.

Notes: The description below contains the technical summary, implementation highlights, and operational guidance. See release_notes field for end-user visible bullets.

review_comments: Ethan Chu (review): Can we make the migration Job tolerant of transient PG connectivity issues? Recommend adding exponential backoff and retries to the runner.
Aisha Patel (author): Added retries with jitter and configurable maxAttempts in runner.go (see commit a1d2f33).
Priya Ramesh (review): The terraform changes need clearer docs on IAM minimal permissions for S3 buckets. Also confirm lifecycle policy doesn't immediately expire snapshots.
Aisha Patel (author): Expanded terraform docs and set default lifecycle to 90 days; added note about retention for compliance in docs/private-installer/upgrade-rollback.md.
Luca Moretti (review): Integration tests were flaky on CI, failure was due to test Postgres resource constraints. Consider running with higher resources or mock the restore step in fast CI lanes.
Aisha Patel (author): Updated CI job to use a larger test instance for the integration workflow and added a fast path that mocks restore for PR-level checks (see ci/integration/upgrade-rollback.yml).
ci_checks: integration-tests: failed (initial run) - migrator race on first attempt
integration-tests: pass (re-run after adding retry/backoff and CI resource bump)
operational_impact: Adds an optional pre-upgrade snapshot step that increases upgrade time (depends on DB size) and requires object storage (S3/GCS) configured. Defaults are conservative: enableTransactionalMigrations=false by default to avoid unexpected changes for existing customers.
rollback_instructions: installer rollback --snapshot-id <id> --verify will attempt to restore the named snapshot into a disposable namespace and run the smoke-check suite. If verification succeeds, operator can run installer rollback --apply to perform a production rollback. See docs/private-installer/upgrade-rollback.md for step-by-step commands and troubleshooting.
release_notes: Private-installer: Add transactional schema migrations with pre-checks and post-checks
Private-installer: Automatic pre-upgrade snapshot (pg_dump) + verified restore to disposable namespace
Private-installer: Downgrade guard that records migration plans and blocks automated downgrade unless a verified path exists
Terraform: optional backup_bucket and IAM policy for automatic snapshots
Helm: pre/post-upgrade hooks to run migrations as a Job; values to enable/disable transactional migrations
CLI: installer migrate --dry-run and installer rollback --verify added for safe operations
notes_for_releaser: Feature is behind a values flag (enableTransactionalMigrations=false). Recommend documenting in upgrade notes and notifying enterprise customers before enabling. Coordinate with SRE to ensure backup_bucket is configured and has correct lifecycle/KMS settings.
testing_summary: Added integration test that runs: deploy vX, take snapshot, apply migrations, verify smoke tests, perform rollback using snapshot, verify restored state. Local unit tests cover runner savepoints and plan_store durability.
risk_acknowledgement: Although migrations try to generate downgrade SQL, not all forward migrations are reversible automatically. The downgrade_guard forces manual approval when a reversible downgrade cannot be generated. Operators must test large migrations in staging before production rollout.
